title: One-term Tor-acyclic K-flat tensor comparison
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and B a commutative R-algebra. Let Q be a cochain complex of R-modules supported only in one degree k, meaning Q^n is zero whenever n is not k. Suppose Tor_i^R(Q^k,B)=0 for every positive integer i [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. For every K-flat R-complex P [def-pc-module-kflat-complex] and quasi-isomorphism f:P\to Q, the termwise tensor map f\otimes_R B:P\otimes_R B\to Q\otimes_R B is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Section 15.60, Lemmas 15.60.7, 15.60.9, 15.60.12 and Definition 15.60.13; parent Tag 08IB final affine calculation

proof.text: The support hypothesis gives IsStrictlyGE k and IsStrictlyLE k. Use Q.isoSingle k to identify Q with the single complex on Q.X k.

Take projectiveResolution of Q.X k and extend its chain complex along embeddingUpIntLE k. Its terms are flat and it is strictly bounded above, so the source-library theorem kFlat_of_isStrictlyLE_of_flat makes it K-flat. For the tensor augmentation at degree zero, map the projective resolution cokernel cofork under tensorRight: mapIsColimit supplies both exactness and epimorphy (Cofork.IsColimit.epi). In positive chain degrees, isoLeftDerivedObj identifies tensor homology with Tor, which vanishes by hypothesis [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Transport this quasi-isomorphism through the extend-functor natural isomorphism and extendSingleIso. Compose using quasiIso_comp with the explicit quasiIso_of_isIso proof for the mapped single-complex isomorphism.

For independence of resolution use the reduced functorial flat resolution Lambda from the source library. kFlat_resolutionFunctor_obj makes every T(X) K-flat and its natural augmentation rho_X is a quasi-isomorphism. Naturality and two-out-of-three make T preserve quasi-isomorphisms. The source-library whiskerRight_of_kFlat lemma, transported through map₂HomologicalComplexFlipObjSingleIso, makes tensorRight N preserve each quasi-isomorphism between these K-flat objects. Apply this first to rho_S and T(g) for the good single resolution to deduce the tensor quasi-isomorphism for rho_Q, then to T(f) and rho_P to deduce it for f. Finally transfer the good single resolution along Q.isoSingle k. This uses strict naturality, with no common-refinement or mixed-scalar tensor theorem.

theorem quasiIso_tensor_of_single_support_tor_acyclic
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra R B]
    (Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (k : ℤ)
    (hsupport : ∀ n : ℤ, n ≠ k → IsZero (Q.X n))
    (hTor : ∀ i : ℕ, 0 < i →
      IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) i).obj (Q.X k)).obj (ModuleCat.of R B)))
    (P : CochainComplex.KFlat (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (f : P.obj ⟶ Q)
    (hf : QuasiIso f) :
    QuasiIso ((((tensoringRight (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj (ModuleCat.of R B)).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map f)
